headline: ARRAS DOUBLES ELEMES DRILL TO 40,000M AFTER $25M RAISE — FOUR RIGS ACTIVE IN KAZAKHSTAN COPPER-GOLD PORPHYRY BELT (TSXV:ARK)
source_name: Investing News Network / Arras Minerals Corp.
snippet: Arras Minerals (TSXV: ARK) announced July 9 that following an upsized C$25 million bought deal financing, it is doubling its 2026 exploration program at the Elemes copper-gold porphyry project in northeastern Kazakhstan to 40,000 metres — with four diamond drill rigs now operating concurrently across targets in the Bozshakol-Chingiz metallogenic belt, approximately 60 km from KAZ Minerals' producing Bozshakol copper-gold mine. The raise and immediate drill-program doubling signals strong institutional conviction built on 30,000+ metres of prior Elemes drilling; in a Kazakhstan that sits at the intersection of Russian supply disruption risk and Western demand for non-Chinese porphyry copper, this is one of the most well-funded pure copper-gold exploration programs advancing under the current commodity supercycle.

headline: DYNACOR STARTS FIRST ORE AT GALAM PILOT PLANT IN SENEGAL — FIRST GOLD POUR TARGET: AUGUST (TSX:DNG)
snippet: Dynacor Group (TSX: DNG) announced July 9 that its Galam pilot plant in the Kédougou region of southeastern Senegal — more than 95% complete, with laboratory and front-end process plant commissioned and in use — has commenced processing first ore on schedule, with hot commissioning ongoing across grinding, leaching, gold refining, and Merrill-Crowe circuits, and first gold pour targeted for August 2026. Kédougou is one of West Africa's highest-grade artisanal gold regions and borders major deposits operated by Endeavour Mining and Barrick; Dynacor's ore-purchasing pilot plant model scales without exploration risk and positions the company as the first formal processor in a district undergoing systematic artisanal gold sector formalization.

headline: SILVER X HITS RECORD Q2: THROUGHPUT +39% QoQ, SILVER +40%, GOLD +55% — NUEVA RECUPERADA AT FULL CAPACITY, 6M AgEq TARGET BY 2029 (TSXV:AGX)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Silver X Mining Corp.
snippet: Silver X Mining (TSXV: AGX) reported July 9 record Q2 2026 production at the Nueva Recuperada property in Peru: 62,252 tonnes processed (+39% QoQ, +78% YoY), silver output up 40% QoQ and 75% YoY, gold up 55% QoQ and 233% YoY — with throughput reaching and sustaining nominal plant capacity as head grades remained broadly stable quarter-over-quarter. Silver X is a rare junior-to-producer graduation story in the silver market: with H1 2026 totalling approximately 463,000 AgEq oz produced and a credible path to approximately 6 million AgEq oz annually by 2029, the company is demonstrating exactly the production growth curve that junior silver investors pay a premium to own at $59+ silver.

headline: ANDINA CONFIRMS THIRD PIUQUENES PORPHYRY: 468M AT 0.50% Cu WITH 164M HIGH-GRADE CORE AT 0.70% Cu — SAN JUAN DISTRICT EXPANDS (CSE:ANDC)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Andina Copper Corp.
snippet: Andina Copper (CSE: ANDC) released July 8 assay results from drillholes PIU12 and PIU13 at Piuquenes North in San Juan Province, Argentina, confirming a third separate porphyry copper-gold system in the district: PIU13 returned 468 metres at 0.50% Cu, 0.30 g/t Au, 3.04 g/t Ag from 700 metres depth, including a 164-metre high-grade core at 0.70% Cu, 0.44 g/t Au from 924 metres, with PIU12 confirming lateral extent across the system. Three separately drilled porphyry systems on a single company's land package in San Juan Province — one of South America's most underexplored copper jurisdictions — transforms Andina from a single-target story into a district-scale copper platform at exactly the moment when $6+/lb copper is incentivizing consolidation.

headline: DPM METALS VARES THROUGHPUT SURGES 48% IN Q2 — 102,000 GEOs ACROSS THREE EUROPEAN MINES, FULL RUN-RATE BY YEAR-END (TSX:DPM)
snippet: DPM Metals (TSX: DPM) reported July 8 Q2 2026 production of approximately 102,000 gold equivalent ounces across Chelopech (~56,000 GEO, Bulgaria), Ada Tepe (~11,000 GEO, Bulgaria), and Vareš (~35,000 GEO, Bosnia-Herzegovina), with the Vareš polymetallic underground mine processing 117,000 tonnes in Q2 — a 48% quarter-on-quarter increase — achieving targeted development rates averaging 400+ metres per month as the paste backfill plant and second tailings filter advance toward the full 850,000 tpa run-rate by year-end 2026. Vareš is one of Europe's most geologically interesting new mines — a volcanogenic massive sulphide system producing gold, silver, zinc, and lead in an EU-accession candidate country, giving it a political and regulatory tailwind that is structurally different from Western European mining risk.

headline: GOLDGROUP WINS FINAL COURT ORDER — $372M MEXICO GOLD MERGER CLOSES JULY 17 AS COMBINED COMPANY TARGETS NYSE AMERICAN LISTING (OTC:GGAZF)
source_name: Investing News Network / Goldgroup Mining Inc.
snippet: Goldgroup Mining received BC Supreme Court final approval on July 6 for its arrangement with Gold Resource Corporation (NYSE American: GORO), clearing the last regulatory hurdle for a US$372 million combination creating a multi-mine, Mexico-focused precious metals producer spanning the Cerro Prieto and San Francisco mines in Sonora, Don David Gold Mine in Oaxaca, and the Back Forty project in Michigan — with closing targeted on or about July 17 following a 4:1 share consolidation to meet NYSE American listing requirements. This consolidation addresses the structural problem that suppressed both companies: neither had the critical mass to attract institutional capital, refinance debt at scale, or fund sustaining capex without continuous equity dilution — a combined 99.99% shareholder vote in favour signals that the market is aligned with the thesis.

headline: SILVER HOLDS $60 AS BOFA CALLS PEAK INDUSTRIAL DEMAND — SIXTH STRAIGHT SUPPLY DEFICIT OF 46M OZ HOLDS THE LINE
snippet: Silver traded in a tight band around $60 per ounce on July 10 as bulls defended a critical technical support zone for a second consecutive week, with Bank of America arguing that industrial silver demand has peaked — accelerating solar panel silver thrifting now outpacing gains from AI data centers, grid modernization, and EVs — while the Silver Institute's 46-million-ounce 2026 supply deficit estimate (the sixth consecutive annual shortfall) provides fundamental support that prevented a break below the $58 floor tested earlier this week. The $60 level is where two structural narratives collide: if BofA's industrial thrifting thesis prevails, silver's industrial premium over gold dissolves and the gold-to-silver ratio widens toward 70:1; if the supply-deficit thesis holds, $60 becomes the base for an H2 recovery.

headline: COPPER FIRMS ON STRAIT OF HORMUZ RISK — BASE METALS MIXED AS GEOPOLITICAL PREMIUM RETURNS TO ENERGY-LINKED COMMODITIES | SP Angel
snippet: SP Angel's July 10 metals market view notes copper trading at $13,526/tonne as U.S. military action near Iran injects a geopolitical risk premium into energy-linked metals — temporarily overriding the LME inventory buildup that Macquarie has identified as the structural bear case through 2027 — with gold holding near $4,100 and base metals broadly mixed as iron ore futures reflect continued China property sector weakness. Copper's dual role as both an industrial bellwether and a geopolitical proxy creates a split in how the Hormuz risk premium allocates: energy disruption scenarios are net-positive for copper substitution in power transmission, while a broader Middle East conflict affecting Chinese manufacturing demand would be the offsetting downside.

headline: FED IS SPLIT 9-TO-8 ON RATE HIKE: GOLD AND SILVER ARE PAYING THE PRICE — UNTIL JULY 14 CPI | GoldSilver.com
snippet: GoldSilver.com's analysis of the recently released FOMC minutes reveals a committee split 9-to-8 on a September 2026 rate hike — the narrowest margin in years — with both gold and silver repricing the increased probability that the Fed tightening cycle isn't finished, pulling metals from recent highs and weighing on mining equities as higher-for-longer expectations expand. The 9-to-8 split makes the July 14 CPI print the single most consequential near-term data point for precious metals: June CPI at or above 4.0% almost certainly locks in a September hike and extends the gold-miner discount, while a sub-3.8% print validates the dovish minority's position and could restore the bull market momentum that carried gold from $3,200 to $5,300 between October 2025 and January 2026.

headline: GOLD MINERS DOWN 15–25% FROM JANUARY HIGHS — ANALYSTS SAY VALUATION DIVERGENCE FROM $4,100 GOLD IS A GENERATIONAL BUY SIGNAL
snippet: A July 2026 analyst round-up on NAI 500 documents the extraordinary divergence between $4,100+ spot gold and mining equity performance: Agnico Eagle Mines (-15.3%), Alamos Gold (-25.6%), Newmont (-14.9%), Barrick Mining (-13.7%), and Kinross Gold (-21.7%) are each at their largest discount to NAV since the 2022–2023 bear market, despite gold holding above $4,100 — with JP Morgan maintaining a $4,800–$6,300 year-end range and Metals Focus targeting $4,920. The structural explanation: this bull market was propelled by price-insensitive central bank buying rather than Western speculative retail flows, which means retail-oriented gold mining equities never got the momentum that historically drags gold stocks higher during a metals bull — and the catch-up trade has yet to materialize.

headline: ALL 18 RARE EARTH ELEMENTS GAINED IN JULY — 16.7% AVERAGE SURGE AS DYSPROSIUM JUMPS 25%, PROJECT VAULT DRIVES SYSTEMATIC U.S. STOCKPILING
snippet: A July 2026 rare earth market review finds all 18 tracked rare earth elements gained simultaneously — averaging 16.7% — led by dysprosium (+25.4%), germanium (+27.8%), and indium (+26.5%) — driven by the Trump administration's Project Vault critical minerals reserve initiative, renewed U.S.-China trade tensions, and growing AI data center demand for heavy rare earth permanent magnets. The breadth of the July rally — all 18 elements rising together rather than isolated individual moves — signals a structural shift from opportunistic price-chasing to systematic stockpiling across the full rare earth suite; historically this broad-based buying pattern has preceded the most durable and largest upward re-ratings of rare earth equity producers and developers.
